description: The AWS Certified AI Practitioner certification validates foundational knowledge of AI/ML concepts, generative AI, and related AWS services. It is designed for individuals who are familiar with, but do not necessarily build, solutions using AI/ML technologies on AWS.

examDetails.unscoredNote: 15 unscored (pretest) questions are included to evaluate future exam items. These are NOT identified on the exam — you must answer all 65 questions as if they count.
examDetails.durationNote: You get 90 minutes (1 hour 30 minutes) to complete the exam. This gives you roughly 1 minute 23 seconds per question.
examDetails.additionalTime: ESL +30 minutes accommodation available for non-native English speakers (request before scheduling).
examDetails.prerequisites: None required. AWS recommends familiarity with AWS Cloud concepts. AWS Cloud Practitioner Essentials or AWS Technical Essentials courses are recommended for those new to AWS.
examDetails.recertification: Retake the AIF-C01 exam OR earn the AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer - Associate credential before expiry.

scoringDetails.passingScoreNote: You need a minimum scaled score of 700 out of 1000 to pass. This is approximately 70% but uses scaled scoring (not a simple percentage).
scoringDetails.scoringModelExplanation: You do NOT need to pass each domain individually. Your overall score across all domains determines if you pass. A strong performance in one domain can compensate for a weaker performance in another.
scoringDetails.scaledScoring: AWS uses a scaled scoring model. Raw scores are converted to a scaled score between 100-1000. The conversion accounts for difficulty differences between exam versions, so passing always represents the same competency level.
scoringDetails.resultDelivery: Pass/Fail result shown immediately on screen. Detailed score report sent via email within 5 business days.
scoringDetails.scoreReport: Your score report shows your overall scaled score and a performance indicator (Meets/Needs Improvement) for each domain.

questionTypes.description: One correct response out of four options (A, B, C, D). This is the most common question type.
questionTypes.tip: Eliminate obviously wrong answers first to improve your odds.

questionTypes.description: Two or more correct responses out of five or more options. The question will specify how many answers to select (e.g., 'Select TWO').
questionTypes.tip: Read carefully how many answers are required. No partial credit — you must select ALL correct answers.

questionTypes.description: Arrange 3-5 responses in the correct sequence to complete a task or process.
questionTypes.tip: Think about the logical flow of the process. Identify the first and last steps, then fill in the middle.

questionTypes.description: Match a list of responses to a list of 3-7 prompts. For example, match AWS services to their descriptions.
questionTypes.tip: Start with the matches you are most confident about, then work through the remaining ones.

domainWeightSummary.lowestWeight: Domains 4 and 5 (14% each) — Still important, don't skip them

strategy: First pass (60 min): Answer all questions you are confident about. Flag uncertain ones for review.
Second pass (20 min): Return to flagged questions. Eliminate wrong answers and make your best choice.
Final review (10 min): Review any remaining flagged questions. Ensure no questions are left unanswered.
NEVER leave a question blank — there is no penalty for guessing.

studyPrioritization.description: Allocate study time roughly proportional to domain weights, but focus more on your weakest areas.

recommended.reason: Highest weight. Covers practical application of FMs, AWS AI services, fine-tuning, RAG, and prompt engineering.
Second highest weight. Covers Bedrock, foundation models, LLMs, and GenAI concepts.

recommended.reason: Core ML concepts that form the foundation for all other domains.

answerTechniques.description: For every question, eliminate obviously wrong answers first. Even eliminating one option improves your odds from 25% to 33%.
AWS exams favor managed services over self-managed solutions. If an option uses a fully managed AWS service vs. a custom implementation, the managed service is usually correct.
Pay attention to keywords: 'MOST cost-effective', 'LEAST operational overhead', 'BEST', 'FIRST'. These qualifiers change the correct answer.
For 'A company wants to...' questions: (1) Identify the requirement, (2) Map it to an AWS service, (3) Choose the simplest solution that meets ALL requirements.
Amazon Bedrock over self-hosted models, SageMaker over EC2, managed services over custom code. AWS exams prefer their managed service offerings.
Never select the first answer that looks right. Read ALL four options before choosing. The best answer might be option D.
Be cautious of options with absolutes like 'always', 'never', 'only', 'all'. These are often incorrect because most AWS services have nuanced use cases.

commonTrapTopics.tip: Bedrock = managed access to foundation models (no ML expertise needed). SageMaker = full ML platform for building/training/deploying custom models.

commonTrapTopics.trap: RAG vs Fine-tuning vs Prompt Engineering
commonTrapTopics.tip: Prompt Engineering = fastest, cheapest, try first. RAG = when you need current/proprietary data without changing the model. Fine-tuning = when you need to change model behavior/style and have labeled data.
Comprehend = NLP text analysis. Rekognition = image/video. Textract = document/OCR. Transcribe = speech-to-text. Polly = text-to-speech. Translate = language translation. Lex = chatbots.
Selection bias = non-representative sample. Measurement bias = flawed data collection. Historical bias = real-world inequalities in data. Confirmation bias = favoring existing beliefs.
Temperature = randomness (higher = more creative). Top-p = cumulative probability threshold. Top-k = number of top tokens to consider. Max tokens = output length limit.
AWS secures infrastructure. YOU secure your data, IAM, encryption settings, model inputs/outputs, and application-level security.

lastMinuteChecklist: Know all AWS AI services and their primary use cases (Rekognition, Comprehend, Transcribe, Polly, Translate, Lex, Textract, Kendra, Personalize, Forecast, Fraud Detector)
Understand Amazon Bedrock: what it is, models available, Knowledge Bases, Agents, Guardrails
Know the ML pipeline: data collection → preprocessing → feature engineering → training → evaluation → deployment → monitoring
Understand fine-tuning vs RAG vs prompt engineering — when to use each
Know inference parameters: temperature, top-p, top-k, max tokens
Understand responsible AI: bias types, SageMaker Clarify, AI Service Cards, explainability (SHAP/LIME)
Know security basics: IAM for Bedrock/SageMaker, VPC, PrivateLink, KMS encryption, CloudTrail logging
Remember: Bedrock does NOT use customer data to train models (data privacy)
Know model evaluation metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC-ROC (classification) and RMSE, MAE (regression)
Understand Amazon Q: Q Business (enterprise search/assistant), Q Developer (coding assistant)

examDayTips: Arrive 15 minutes early if testing at a Pearson VUE center
For online proctored: test your system requirements beforehand, ensure quiet room with clear desk
Bring two forms of valid ID (testing center) or have one ready (online)
Read each question TWICE before answering
Flag difficult questions and come back — don't waste 5 minutes on one question
Answer every single question — no penalty for wrong answers
Trust your first instinct unless you find a clear reason to change your answer
Use the strike-through feature to eliminate wrong answers visually
If two answers seem correct, choose the one that is MORE specific to the question's requirements
Take a deep breath if you feel rushed — 90 minutes is enough if you manage time well
